name: Platform mounds with sunken circular plazas on the Peruvian coast
summary: People on Peru's north-central coast built stone platforms with sunken circular plazas between 3500 and 3000 BCE, a form that came to define the region's early monumental architecture.
description: At Sechin Bajo in the Casma Valley, builders raised a platform of stones set in clay, at least 40 metres long and over two metres high, with a stair down to a sunken circular plaza about 16 metres across; radiocarbon samples place it between 3500 and 3000 BC. The excavators say such plazas later became a defining feature of early monumental architecture in the region. In the Fortaleza and Pativilca valleys of the Norte Chico, Haas, Creamer and Ruiz dated a Late Archaic complex of more than 20 large sites sharing large-scale monumental architecture to between 3000 and 1800 calibrated years BC.

impact.note: The form shaped ceremonial centres of coastal Peru for many centuries, one region's societies (reach 1); organised building far beyond dwelling scale was a new capability there (depth 2); later centres repeated and enlarged the platform and sunken plaza, a line of direct successors (generativity 1), and wider Andean descent is not shown by the sources opened.

events.statement: Ninety-five radiocarbon dates place a major Late Archaic cultural complex in the Norte Chico region between 3000 and 1800 calibrated years BC.

evidence.supports: The 95 new dates confirm the emergence and development of a major cultural complex in this region during the Late Archaic period between 3000 and 1800 calibrated calendar years bc
evidence.locator: Abstract; the preceding sentence says the dated sites share large-scale monumental architecture

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The Sechin Bajo dates rest on the excavating university's press release; the excavation report (Fuchs and colleagues, 2009) should replace it.
Sechin Bajo and Norte Chico coordinates were entered from memory and not taken from a fetched source.
The Caral dates and the lead's 2600 BCE end-date were not checked against a fetched source.
Whether the Casma and Norte Chico building traditions were connected, and which came first, is not settled by the sources opened.

research.note: Contact with Old World builders was impossible at this date, and the excavators call Sechin Bajo one of the oldest ceremonial sites of the Americas; the sources do not say it was the first in the Andes, and its relation to other early Andean centres is open.
